building.name: Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR, Tenth Edition, Base Volume (2021 International Building Code with Massachusetts amendments)
building.local_amendments_note: Worcester has no building code of its own: 780 CMR is 'the building code for all towns, cities' and the city's ordinances charge the building commissioner with enforcing 'the state building code'. The one local choice is on energy: Worcester adopted the Stretch Code (May 4, 2010) and the Specialized opt-in energy code (voted September 26, 2023, in effect July 1, 2024), which do not touch toilet partitions.
building.effective: 2024-10-11 (Mass. Register Issue 1532). The state code record says the period in which the Ninth Edition could still be used ended June 30, 2025; that date was not read on an official page.
building.quote: 780 CMR 101.1: 'The Board of Building Regulations and Standards ("BBRS") adopts and incorporates by reference, the International Building Code-2021 ("IBC") ... These, together with modifications as set forth, shall collectively comprise 780 CMR, otherwise known as the Massachusetts State Building Code, Tenth Edition, Base Volume.' | 780 CMR 101.2: '780 CMR shall be the building code for all towns, cities, state agencies or authorities in accordance with M.G.L. c. 143, §§ 93 through 100.' (both: 'Amended by Mass Register Issue 1532, eff. 10/11/2024') | Worcester Revised Ordinances of 2015, Part Two, Inspectional Services, § 7(b)(1): the building commissioner shall '(A) administer and enforce the state building code pursuant to chapter one hundred forty three of the General Laws and the regulations adopted pursuant thereto; (B) administer and enforce the provisions of the architectural access board ...'

fixtures.note: Toilet counts come from the state's Uniform State Plumbing Code (248 CMR 10.10 Table 1), which counts seats and staff, not floor area; the state pack's worked examples stand. Worcester's Revised Ordinances (Part One as amended through September 8, 2026, and Part Two) were searched in full for 'toilet', 'restroom', 'bathroom', 'unisex', 'gender neutral', 'plumbing': nothing sets or changes toilet counts, the men's and women's split, urinals or the small-business exception. The only local plumbing text is on sewers and grease traps.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 780 CMR 105.1: 'It shall be unlawful to construct, reconstruct, alter, repair, remove or demolish a building or structure; or to change the use or occupancy of a building or structure; or to install or alter any equipment or life safety systems for which provision is made or the installation of which is regulated by 780 CMR without first filing an application with the building official and obtaining the required permit.' | 780 CMR 105.2: 'While other kinds of permits may be required for work governed by other laws, by-laws, rules and the specialized codes of M.G.L. c. 143, § 96, such as electrical, plumbing, and sheet metal, a permit pursuant to 780 CMR is not required for the following activities: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area is not greater than 120 ft.2 2. Fences not over seven feet high. 3. Oil derricks. 4. Retaining walls that are not over four feet in height ... 5. Water tanks supported directly on grade ... 6. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches above adjacent grade ... 7. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. 8. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 9. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy ... 10. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes ... 11. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. 12. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies ... 13. Non-fixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over five feet nine inches (1,753 mm) in height. 14. Greenhouses covered exclusively with plastic film. ... 15. Repair of any component or components of a fire protection system ...' | 105.2.2: 'Repairs. Application or notice to the building official is not required for ordinary repairs to structures. A permit is required for work including but not limited to: the substantial cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements or mechanical systems or other work affecting public health or general safety under the jurisdiction of 780 CMR.' | City of Worcester, Building & Zoning: 'Alterations/Renovations: Authorizes changes or improvements within the existing building footprint such as modifying layouts, finishes, or building systems – without expanding the structure's size or adding new floor area.' ... 'Any person working without proper permits or licenses shall be subject to a fine of $500.00 for residential properties or $1000.00 for commercial properties. In addition to the proper permit or license fee.'
permit.partitions_named_note: Item 13 names 'non-fixed and movable ... partitions not over five feet nine inches'; toilet partitions fixed to the floor, wall or ceiling are not named, and neither the state list nor the city's page says whether replacing them is finish work, an ordinary repair or an alteration. The city publishes no exempt-work list of its own beyond FAQ answers on sheds, fences and retaining walls.
permit.office: City of Worcester Building and Zoning Division, Inspectional Services, 25 Meade Street

restrooms_city.rule: No ordinance applies to private buildings. A city manager's executive order of September 8, 2020 covers buildings owned by the City of Worcester, school buildings included: each publicly facing city-owned building must have at least one 'inclusive bathroom' (a single-user toilet room open to any gender, with a lock) by December 31, 2022, with a sign at its entrance identifying it.
restrooms_city.quote: § 2. POLICY ... A. Each publicly facing City-owned building shall have at least one inclusive bathroom by December 31, 2022. B. Each inclusive bathroom shall bear a sign, which shall be plainly viewable at its entrance identifying it as an inclusive bathroom. C. An inclusive bathroom shall be a single-user toilet facility designated for use by no more than one occupant at a time or for family or assisted use. D. As used in this Order, the term "inclusive bathroom" includes, but is not limited to, a bathroom facility that is available for use regardless of gender (e.g., male, female, non-binary) or sex (e.g., man, woman, intersex). E. As used in this Order, the term "single-user facility" means a toilet facility with no more than one water closet and one urinal with a locking mechanism controlled by the user.
restrooms_city.note: Read as a scanned one-page PDF on the city's open data portal (item listed there as signed by the former city manager; record last modified July 2024). Whether a later order replaced it was not checked. The Revised Ordinances contain no rule on restroom signs or all-gender rooms.

public_wage.city_rule: Responsible Employer Ordinance (Worcester Revised Ordinances of 2008, Chapter 2, § 35, ordained September 18, 2012): on city building construction contracts, which the city's bid form applies to contracts over $100,000, every bidder and subcontractor must certify under oath that it pays the state prevailing wage, maintains a state-approved apprentice training program, carries workers' compensation, classifies workers as employees, has OSHA 10-hour trained workers and keeps a daily sign-in and sign-out log. page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Worcester job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Massachusetts rules Worcester enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Worcester colleges, hospitals, public schools and office buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Massachusetts sets the number of toilets by the people a building is set up for, and Worcester applies the state's count without changes of its own. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Worcester enforces the Massachusetts building rules, which require a permit to alter or repair a building and list the work that needs none. The list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. Ordinary repairs need no permit either. The list doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask Worcester's Building and Zoning Division (508-799-1198) whether your replacement needs one. Worcester fines work done without a required permit, $1,000 on a commercial property. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Massachusetts lets men's and women's toilets be replaced by single-user rooms open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in a lockable compartment with partitions from floor to ceiling and a single-user room open to everyone is on the same floor within 300 feet. When an existing room is converted, partitions that lock may stay, but new ones must be full height. Where restrooms are separated by sex, state law lets each person use the one that matches their gender identity. Worcester adds a rule for its own buildings only: under a 2020 order by the city manager, each city-owned building open to the public must have at least one single-user restroom open to everyone, with a sign at its entrance.
page.confirm_office: Worcester's Building and Zoning Division at Inspectional Services
page.install_rule: Worcester asks for the contractor's trade license and proof of workers' compensation insurance to be on file with Inspectional Services or attached to the permit application. Massachusetts has no general contractor license for commercial interior work, but work that needs a building permit may have to be supervised by a licensed construction supervisor, so check with Worcester's Building and Zoning Division before work starts. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Where a permit is needed, Worcester asks for the contractor's license and workers' compensation proof with the application.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county, city, town and school district construction, Massachusetts law requires at least the wage rates the state Department of Labor Standards sets for that project, with no minimum project size in the law. The state issues the rates project by project, so there is no standing rate table. On a schedule issued in November 2026 for a City of Worcester project, a carpenter is listed at $52.10 an hour plus $31.05 in benefits, rising to $53.35 an hour on March 1, 2027. On city building contracts over $100,000, Worcester also requires every bidder and subcontractor to certify that it pays the prevailing wage, takes part in a state-approved apprentice program and keeps a daily sign-in log.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.25% in Worcester. That is Massachusetts's state rate, and no city or county sales tax on goods was found.
page.buyers_extra: - **Colleges and hospitals:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE where student traffic is hard on stalls.

Sales tax: the Department of Revenue's pages would not open; the 6.25% rate and its August 1, 2009 start were read in the statute and the 2009 act on the legislature's site.
